bull.t: Recurring subscription momentum and high retention
bull.b: Strong subscription growth and 108% NRR indicate durable revenue predictability and customer expansion. A rising base of large clients (> $100k) and healthy retention reduce churn risk, support recurring cash flows, and enable cross-sell of higher‑margin modules over multiple quarters.

High gross and operating margins with strong operating and free cash flow underpin reinvestment and capital returns. Durable cash conversion supports funding AI investments, strategic M&A, buybacks, and debt reduction while preserving operating flexibility over the medium term.

Board continuity and auditor ratification signal stable governance and investor alignment. Consistent oversight and shareholder backing reduce execution risk for multi-year initiatives, aiding strategic consistency and credibility with large healthcare provider customers and institutional investors.

bear.b: A $1.5B gross debt load with mid‑single‑digit net leverage constrains financial flexibility if growth slows. Debt servicing and covenant risk could limit acquisition funding or require slower buyback pacing, increasing sensitivity to operating volatility over the next several quarters.

Slower volume-based and overall revenue growth reduces operating leverage potential and may pressure long-term margin expansion. Reliance on subscription expansion to offset volume weakness increases execution risk and heightens importance of sustained cross-sell and retention efforts.

bear.t: Rising AI/software investment and cash flow variability
bear.b: Material increases in capitalized software and AI compute costs raise the breakeven for new offerings and can depress near-term FCF conversion. If revenue benefits take longer to materialize, these elevated investments could compress free cash flow and slow deleveraging over multiple quarters.
